This is a genuine gap in the existing taxonomy for ML/AI-native repositories where eval infrastructure is first-class engineering work. All other code in this repository maps cleanly to the eight existing categories.

### 9. Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

The existing eight categories cover the code well with one exception: the `tests/eval/`, `tests/test_eval_*.py`, `tests/test_bench_*.py`, and the `eval/` directory contain files that are **neither production tests nor benchmarks in the traditional sense** — they are empirical evaluation harnesses (gold-standard generation, nDCG@10 runs, judge calibration, extraction quality scoring). These sit ambiguously between "test generation" and "feature" (they encode new analytical methodology). If the taxonomy needs to distinguish them:

> **Proposed addition: `evaluation_harness`** — code whose primary output is a metric or quality signal rather than a correctness assertion or user-facing capability. Evidenced by [`eval/build_gold_standard.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/sjarmak-scix-agent@dd618037f61035bd62f1e7a620029c6b4867ab6a/-/blob/eval/build_gold_standard.py), `tests/test_eval_retrieval_50q.py`, `tests/test_bench_pgvectorscale*.py`, `tests/test_calibrate_judge.py`, etc.

This is a genuine gap in the existing taxonomy for ML/AI-native repositories where eval infrastructure is first-class engineering work. All other code in this repository maps cleanly to the eight existing categories.
